When completed, it will be [[High-speed rail in India|India's first high-speed rail line]], with a design speed of {{convert|350|km/h|abbr=on|round=5}},{{Cite web |last=Rao |first=Shashank |date=22 September 2024 |title=First bullet train will arrive from Japan in 2 years |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/first-bullet-train-will-arrive-from-japan-in-2-years-101726945881769.html |access-date=2 December 2024 |website=Hindustan Times}}{{cite web|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2015-06-23/news/63746148_1_feasibility-study-jica-bullet-train-project|title=JICA presents draft report on bullet train project to joint committee|work=timesofindia-economictimes|access-date=16 July 2015|archive-date=27 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827001545/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2015-06-23/news/63746148_1_feasibility-study-jica-bullet-train-project|url-status=dead}} and the project will include a {{cvt|353|km|mi|adj=mid|-long}} viaduct, which will be the [[List of longest bridges|longest bridge in the world]]. The line is being developed by the [[National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited]] (NHSRCL), a wholly owned [[subsidiary]] of [[Indian Railways]], the [[Ministry of Railways (India)|Ministry of Railways]], and the [[Government of India]]. The line will use [[Shinkansen]] technology from [[Japan]], including rolling stock, signalling and design standards – with technology transfer to support the [[Make in India]] programme. After delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, construction commenced in February 2021, when the NHSRCL began to pour concrete to cast the corridor's first pillar.{{Cite web|date=10 February 2021|title=L&T Begins Pier Work for Mumbai - Ahmedabad Bullet Train|url=https://themetrorailguy.com/2021/02/10/lt-begins-pier-work-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train/|access-date=2 October 2021|website=The Metro Rail Guy|language=en-US|archive-date=11 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211063359/https://themetrorailguy.com/2021/02/10/lt-begins-pier-work-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train/|url-status=live}} An initial section between [[Surat high-speed railway station|Surat]] and [[Bilimora high-speed railway station|Bilimora]] in Gujarat, is planned to open for service on 15 August 2027, with the full line to open by 2029.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-01-01 |title=First Bullet train ride between Surat to Bilimora in 2027: Check routes, fares & other details |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/railway-minister-shares-timeline-for-india-first-bullet-train-surat-bilimora-section-august-2027-101767265883374.html |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=[[Hindustan Times]]}} ==History== ===Conception=== The Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor, along with five other high-speed rail corridors, was reintroduced for a [[feasibility study]] in the 2009–2010 [[Rail Budget]]. Multiple such feasibility studies had been carried out earlier. A {{cvt|650|km|adj=on}} long high-speed rail corridor was proposed to run from {{stnlnk|Pune}} to {{stnlnk|Ahmedabad}} via Mumbai. The point at which this route would touch Mumbai was to be decided when the feasibility report was prepared. The pre-feasibility study for the Ahmedabad–Mumbai–Pune corridor was completed by a consortium of [[RITES]], Italferr, and [[Systra]].{{cite web|last1=Thakur|first1=Raghav|title=Indian high-speed project moves forward|url=http://www.railjournal.com/index.php/asia/indian-high-speed-rail-project-moves-forward.html|website=www.railjournal.com|access-date=18 April 2016|date=10 September 2012|archive-date=28 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428155408/http://www.railjournal.com/index.php/asia/indian-high-speed-rail-project-moves-forward.html|url-status=live}} The top speed expected for the corridor was set up to {{cvt|350|km/h}}.{{Cite web |url=http://www.jterc.or.jp/koku/koku_semina/pdf/130211-jic-presentation.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=11 October 2013 |archive-date=18 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918150119/http://www.jterc.or.jp/koku/koku_semina/pdf/130211-jic-presentation.pdf |url-status=dead }} The proposed stations included [[Lonavala]] on the [[Mumbai]]–[[Pune]] section, and [[Surat]], [[Bharuch]], and [[Vadodara]] on the Mumbai–Ahmedabad section. It was proposed to have 32 services between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. Railway officials also proposed extending the corridor up to [[Bengaluru]].{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Extend-high-speed-corridor-up-to-Bangalore/articleshow/11454940.cms|title=Extend high-speed corridor up to Bangalore|work=The Times of India|date=12 January 2012|access-date=13 January 2012|archive-date=9 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170109200738/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Extend-high-speed-corridor-up-to-Bangalore/articleshow/11454940.cms|url-status=live}} A [[memorandum of understanding|Memorandum of Understanding]] (MoU) was signed in [[New Delhi]] on 14 February 2013, between the [[Ministry of Railways (India)|Ministry of Railways]] and the [[SNCF|Société Nationale des Chemins de Fer Français]] (SNCF), the [[French National Railway Company|French national railways]], for [[Technical Cooperation Program|technical cooperation]] in the field of railways. The parties agreed to carry out jointly an "operations and development" feasibility project on the Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor. The project was funded by the SNCF with support from the [[French Ministry of Finance]]. In March 2013, the [[Railway Board]] decided to drop the Mumbai–Pune section and operate the high-speed rail service only between Mumbai and Ahmedabad. The Board decided, due to financial constraints, that the [[Western Ghats|Ghat section]] between Pune and Mumbai would escalate the budget for the project. According to Vidyadhar A. Malegaonkar, Chief [[Public relations officer|Public Relations Officer]] (PRO), [[Western Railway zone|Western Railway]], "It's a Western Railway project and a very small portion of Maharashtra was being covered under it. Hence, the [[Government of Maharashtra|Maharashtra government]] was showing little interest in the project and was also reluctant to bear a financial burden. That is the reason why the [[Railway Board]] has decided against including the Pune–Mumbai portion in the high-speed corridor".{{Cite web|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/punemumbai-section-dropped-from-high-speed-rail-corridor-plan/1086191/0|title=Pune–Mumbai section dropped from high-speed rail corridor plan|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=30 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230014940/http://www.indianexpress.com/news/punemumbai-section-dropped-from-high-speed-rail-corridor-plan/1086191/0|url-status=live}} India and [[Japan]] signed a [[Memorandum of understanding|MoU]] to undertake a joint feasibility study of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad route in New Delhi in September 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalturk.com/en/india-japan-sign-mou-for-feasibility-study-of-high-speed-railway-system-in-india-43654|title=India, Japan sign MoU for a feasibility study for a high-speed railway system in India|date=9 October 2013|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=13 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131013141250/http://www.nationalturk.com/en/india-japan-sign-mou-for-feasibility-study-of-high-speed-railway-system-in-india-43654|url-status=live}} This was in pursuance of the [[Join statement|Joint Statement]] between the then-[[Prime Minister of India]], [[Manmohan Singh]], and the [[Prime Minister of Japan]], [[Shinzō Abe]], on 29 May 2013, which provided that the two sides would co-finance a joint feasibility study of the route. The objective of the joint study was to prepare a feasibility report of the system with a speed of {{cvt|300 to 350|km/h}}. The cost of the study (¥500 million){{cite web|url=http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/high-speed/single-view/view/feasibility-study-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-line-agreed.html?sword_list%5B%5D=india&no_cache=1|title=Feasibility study for Mumbai – Ahmedabad high-speed line agreed|author=DVV Media UK|work=Railway Gazette|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=27 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127030618/http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/high-speed/single-view/view/feasibility-study-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-line-agreed.html?sword_list%5B%5D=india&no_cache=1|url-status=dead}} was borne equally by India and Japan The study was scheduled to be completed within 18 months from its [[commencement]], i.e., by July 2015. The study carried out [[traffic forecasting]], and alignment surveys and undertook a comparative study of [[high-speed railway technology]] and systems.{{cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=102208|title=Press Information Bureau|access-date=26 January 2014|archive-date=22 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922051851/http://pib.nic.in/newsite/erelease.aspx?relid=102208|url-status=live}}{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ani/india-japan-discuss-possiblity-to-implement-high-speed-railways-system-in-india-114012500870_1.html|title=India, Japan discuss {{sic|possi|blity|nolink=y}} to implement High Speed Railways system in India|author=ANI|date=25 January 2014|newspaper=Business Standard India|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=22 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922100140/http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ani/india-japan-discuss-possiblity-to-implement-high-speed-railways-system-in-india-114012500870_1.html|url-status=live}} [[Japan International Cooperation Agency]] (JICA) and the SNCF carried out studies on the project. JICA researched the technology, alignment, and traffic-related aspects, while SNCF worked on business projections.{{Cite news |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-government-readying-to-open-up-some-railway-segments-to-fdi-1948452 |title=Government readying to open up some railway segments to FDI |date=10 January 2014|work=Daily News & Analysis|access-date=7 February 2018 |archive-date=22 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922071848/http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-government-readying-to-open-up-some-railway-segments-to-fdi-1948452|url-status=live}} The feasibility study included an alignment survey concerning aspects such as [[Land acquisition in India|land acquisition]], [[Environmental Challenges|environmental challenges]], and the building of [[tunnel]]s and [[bridge]]s. It also suggested a financial model based on fare and non-fare box revenue.{{cite news |title=Mumbai–Ahmedabad high speed corridor proposed via Thane |work=The Times of India |date=26 January 2014 |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbai-Ahmedabad-high-speed-corridor-proposed-via-Thane/articleshow/29379878.cms|access-date=26 January 2014 |url-status=live |archive-date=12 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112183328/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Mumbai-Ahmedabad-high-speed-corridor-proposed-via-Thane/articleshow/29379878.cms}} ===Planning=== JICA officials visited Mumbai in January 2014 to discuss the details of the project and made selective site visits to the proposed route. On 21 January, following several meetings between JICA and [[Indian Railways]] officials, it was proposed to originate the corridor at the [[Bandra Kurla Complex]] (BKC) in Mumbai. The proposed route would begin from BKC, go right up to [[Thane]] on the [[Central Line (Mumbai Suburban Railway)|Central Line]], and then take a diversion on the [[Trans-Harbour Line (Mumbai Suburban Railway)|Trans-Harbour route]], which is on the Thane-[[Diva Junction railway station|Diva]]-[[Vasai Road railway station|Vasai]]-[[Virar high-speed railway station|Virar]] stretch. The corridor would then switch over to the [[Western Line (Mumbai Suburban Railway)|Western Line]], before entering Gujarat and terminating at Ahmedabad.{{cite web|url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/railways-planning-320-kmph-bkc-ahmedabad-corridor/15043022|title=Railways planning 320 kmph BKC-Ahmedabad corridor|date=27 January 2014|work=mid-day|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=25 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425173717/http://www.mid-day.com/articles/railways-planning-320-kmph-bkc-ahmedabad-corridor/15043022|url-status=live}} 12 stations were proposed on the route, of which 8 would have been in Gujarat. The intention behind taking the route via Thane is to keep the option open to link the corridor to Pune. The team also proposed other options for originating the line at either [[Bandra Terminus]] or [[Lokmanya Tilak Terminus]], if the BKC option was unfeasible. Air-conditioned bullet trains are expected to operate in the corridor at speeds of {{cvt|320|km/h}}, enabling commuters to traverse the {{cvt|534|km}} distance in two hours. Currently, the fastest train operating in this sector is the [[Ahmedabad-Mumbai Central Vande Bharat Express|Ahmedabad-Mumbai Vande Bharat Express]], which takes 5 hours and 40 minutes to reach {{stnlnk|Mumbai Central}} from Ahmedabad, running non-stop between these two cities at a maximum speed of {{cvt|130|km/h}}. The project held its first full-fledged meeting at the Railway Ministry in the first week of April 2014 to bring about a broad consensus on the project, especially between the governments of Maharashtra and Gujarat. The meeting was attended by representatives from the Maharashtra and Gujarat governments, the JICA, and the Railway Board officials. At the meeting, officials agreed to begin the line from BKC, and then take it to Thane and onward to Virar. The Maharashtra government was in favour of connecting the line with [[CBD Belapur|Belapur]] as well, to bring high-speed rail to [[Navi Mumbai]]. However, railway officials were opposed to the Belapur detour. Officials also discussed the need to ensure that the terminal at BKC would be connected to [[Line 3 (Mumbai Metro)|Line 3]] of the [[Mumbai Metro]], enabling commuters from [[South Mumbai]] to reach BKC. web|url=http://www.ndtv.com/mumbai-news/mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train-may-run-on-elevated-corridor-1263467 |title=Mumbai–Ahmedabad Bullet Train May Run On Elevated Corridor|author=Press Trust of news|url=http://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/english/news/20150721_01.html|title=India:Japan system best for its high-speed train |publisher=NHK WORLD News|date=20 July 2015|access-date=22 July 2015|archive-date=22 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150722142304/http://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/english/news/20150721_01.html|url-status=dead}} JICA's report recommended constructing 63.3% of the route an embankment slightly above the ground, 28.3% on stilts, 5.8% underground, and 2.2% on bridges. Minister of State for Railways [[Rajen Gohain]] informed [[Parliament of India|Parliament]] on 15 March 2017 that under a new plan, the entire corridor would be elevated except for the tracks that were proposed to be built underground.{{cite web |title=Mum-Ahmedabad rail corridor to be fully elevated, says Rajen Gohain|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mum-ahmedabad-rail-corridor-to-be-fully-elevated-says-rajen-gohain-2355744|website=dna|access-date=17 March 2017|date=17 March 2017|archive-date=18 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318071016/http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mum-ahmedabad-rail-corridor-to-be-fully-elevated-says-rajen-gohain-2355744|url-status=live}} The Ministry of Railways, based on the recommendation of the [[NITI Aayog]], announced that [[Shinkansen]] technology would be adopted for the line, with technology transfer to support the [[Make in India]] programme. Japan would also provide staff training.{{cite web|url=http://www.railwaygazette.com/news/single-view/view/india-and-japan-sign-high-speed-rail-memorandum.html|title=India and Japan sign high-speed rail memorandum|author=DVV Media UK|work=Railway Gazette|access-date=4 March 2016|archive-date=15 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515220129/https://www.railwaygazette.com/india-and-japan-sign-high-speed-rail-memorandum/41785.article|url-status=live}} In January 2016, the Ministry of Railways fast-tracked the project and set up a [[Special Purpose Vehicle]] (SPV) named the National High-Speed Rail Corporation Limited to build and operate the corridor. The company was registered in January 2016 in the name of Indian Railways. It was planned for the company to eventually be made into a joint venture, with equity participation of the Maharashtra and Gujarat governments. The public sector company is expected to build and also carry out train operations.{{cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Railways-fast-tracks-Mumbai-Ahmedabad-bullet-train-project-sets-up-separate-company/articleshow/50432014.cms|title=Railways fast-tracks Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train project, sets up separate company|work=The Times of India|date=4 January 2016|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=11 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111005105/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Railways-fast-tracks-Mumbai-Ahmedabad-bullet-train-project-sets-up-separate-company/articleshow/50432014.cms|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-railways-forms-special-purpose-vehicle-to-execute-mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train-project-2186638|title=Railways forms Special Purpose Vehicle to execute Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train project|date=7 March 2016|work=dna|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-date=13 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313215408/http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-railways-forms-special-purpose-vehicle-to-execute-mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train-project-2186638|url-status=live}} The Ministry of Railways, the National High-Speed Rail Corporation (NHSRCL){{cite web|url=https://www.nhsrcl.in/|title=National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited|website=National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited|access-date=13 June 2019|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601010612/https://www.nhsrcl.in/|url-status=live}} and JICA signed a tripartite consultancy agreement in December 2016 to implement the project. The NHSRCL, was a new agency floated to implement the project. A joint venture between Japan International Consultants for Transportation Co (JIC), [[Nippon Koei]] Co, and Oriental Consultants Global Co. Ltd. was appointed as the general consultants for the project,{{cite news|title=JICA inks pact for Mumbai–Ahmedabad high speed rail project|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/jica-inks-pact-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-project/articleshow/56107569.cms|newspaper=The Economic Times|access-date=9 April 2017|date=21 December 2016|archive-date=9 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409113543/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/jica-inks-pact-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-project/articleshow/56107569.cms|url-status=live}} and prepared design documents, bidding documents and technical standards and specifications for the project. In late 2016, JICA awarded the detailed design study for the project to a consortium led by Japan International Consultants for Transportation (JIC), Nippon Koei India Pvt. Ltd, and Oriental Consultants. The study formally began in March 2017. JIC will forecast demand, set fares, and devise a train operation plan, handle preliminary design work for structures such as tunnels and bridges, and draw up an overall construction schedule. The Japan International Consultants for Transportation (JIC) Project Manager stated that "conditions surrounding the construction of a high-speed railway in India – such as weather, which is harsh there, and the quality and standards of materials – are considerably different from those in Japan. So we are now comparing and adjusting to these technical matters." Japanese public and private sector companies conducted training programs for railway staff in India. JIC stated that the local expertise in India gained from constructing and operating various rapid transit systems could be utilised for the high-speed rail project. Japan also provided training to Indian Railway Ministry officials, some of whom studied in government-sponsored programs at graduate schools in Japan. India and Japan signed an agreement to establish an HSR Training Institute in India by 2020 to train railway staff in high-speed rail operations.{{cite web|last1=Yamada|first1=Gp|title=India's first bullet train project gets going|url=http://asia.nikkei.com/Politics-Economy/International-Relations/India-s-first-bullet-train-project-gets-going|website=Nikkei Asian Review|access-date=17 March 2017|date=17 March 2017|archive-date=17 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170317150347/http://asia.nikkei.com/Politics-Economy/International-Relations/India-s-first-bullet-train-project-gets-going|url-status=live}} The project received clearance from the [[National Board for Wildlife]] (NBWL) in January 2019 to carry out construction in and around the wildlife areas. The Board required the NHSRCL to create safe passages for animals to pass through before beginning construction, and to erect noise barriers and fencing to prevent any disturbance to wildlife during construction.{{cite web |title=First build safe animal passages, then lay bullet train lines: Wildlife board |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/first-build-safe-animal-passages-then-lay-bullet-train-lines-wildlife-board/story-d7IaSNAisN8zlPGdKWjNpK.html |website=Hindustan Times |access-date=26 January 2019 |date=24 January 2019 |archive-date=26 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126113829/https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/first-build-safe-animal-passages-then-lay-bullet-train-lines-wildlife-board/story-d7IaSNAisN8zlPGdKWjNpK.html |url-status=live }} The project received conditional clearance to cut down 53,467 mangrove trees, spread over an area of 13.36 hectares{{cite web |title=MoEF cleared plan to cut 53,467 mangrove trees, Bombay high court told |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/moef-cleared-plan-to-cut-53-467-mangrove-trees-bombay-high-court-told/story-OYw5ZD6bIVMtzqcpJrt5aP.html |website=Hindustan Times |access-date=23 September 2019 |date=9 April 2019 |archive-date=23 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190923061708/https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/moef-cleared-plan-to-cut-53-467-mangrove-trees-bombay-high-court-told/story-OYw5ZD6bIVMtzqcpJrt5aP.html |url-status=live }} from the expert appraisal committee (EAC) on Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) projects of the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests on 18 March 2019. The Ministry required the NHSRCL to obtain approval from the Bombay High Court and clearance from the Dahanu Taluka Environment Protection Authority. The depots were designed based on the operations at Japan's [[Sendai]] and [[Kanazawa]] depots for Shinkansen. The Sabarmati depot is spread over an area of 80 hectares and serves as the main depot for the line. It also houses the operation control centre for the corridor. The Thane depot is spread over an area of 60 hectares. The Sabarmati and Thane depots contain washing plants, inspection bays, sheds, workshops, and stabling lines for regular maintenance of trains. The Surat depot is the smallest, with an area of 44 hectares. It contains basic facilities for train maintenance. All depots contain reservoirs for rainwater harvesting, and collected water is passed through treatment plants within the depot before being reused for washing trainsets. Depots also have recharge pits for recharging water back into the earth. The Thane and Surat depots are also capable of recycling and reusing effluent and sewage water. Bio-waste from the trains is stored in tanks onboard and removed at depots, where it is then treated in sewage treatment plants.{{cite web |title=Wonderful step! Later on 6 October, NHSRCL had successfully erected the first steel bridge, measuring {{cvt|70|m}}, over [[National Highway 53 (India)|National Highway 53]] in Surat in Gujarat; this bridge was the first among the 28 steel bridges planned for the corridor.{{Cite news |date=6 October 2023 |title=NHSRCL erects first steel bridge for Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail Corridor |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/nhsrcl-erects-first-steel-bridge-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-corridor/articleshow/104215171.cms |url-status=live |access-date=28 November 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20231219035621/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/nhsrcl-erects-first-steel-bridge-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-corridor/articleshow/104215171.cms |archive-date=19 December 2023 |issn=0971-8257}} ===2024=== On 8 January, the land acquisition for the entire corridor was completed.{{cite web |title=100 per cent land acquisition completed for Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project: NHSRCL |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2024/jan/08/100-per-cent-land-acquisition-completed-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train-project-nhsrcl-2649101.html |website=The New Indian Express |date=8 January 2024 |access-date=10 March 2024}} On 16 January, L&T was awarded package no. EW-1 of the project, which involves electrification works across its entire {{convert|508|km|mi}} length. The scope of this package includes commissioning a 2 x 25 kV [[Overhead line|overhead electrification system]] to enable the line's trains to operate up to speeds of up to 320 km/hour, and also designing and commissioning traction substations, switching substations, distribution systems, associated buildings, and training institute equipment for the entire corridor and 3 depots located in [[Thane]], [[Surat]] and [[Sabarmati]].{{cite web |url=https://www.larsentoubro.com/pressreleases/2024-01-16-lt-construction-railway-business-group-awarded-mega-order-to-build-electrification-system-for-the-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-project/ |title=L&T Construction's Railway Business Group awarded (Mega*) order to build Electrification System Works for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Project |date=16 January 2024 |website=larsentoubro.com |publisher=Larsen & Toubro |access-date=21 January 2024 |archive-date=23 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240323021805/https://www.larsentoubro.com/pressreleases/2024-01-16-lt-construction-railway-business-group-awarded-mega-order-to-build-electrification-system-for-the-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-project/ |url-status=live }} On 19 April, NHSRCL completed 300 km of pier work on the bullet train corridor.{{Cite web |title=India's 1st Bullet Train: Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor achieves another milestone! Check latest update |url=https://www.etnownews.com/infrastructure/indias-1st-bullet-train-mumbai-ahmedabad-high-speed-rail-corridor-achieves-another-milestone-check-latest-update-article-109367855 |access-date=19 April 2024 |website=ET NOW |date=19 April 2024 |language=en}} As of July 2024, work began on the 7 km undersea tunnel section across Thane Creek and 194 km of viaduct construction had been completed.{{Cite web |date=17 July 2024 |title=Bullet Train Project: NHSRCL begins construction work on 7-km undersea rail tunnel – Check Mumbai station construction details here |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways-bullet-train-project-nhsrcl-begins-construction-work-on-7-km-undersea-rail-tunnel-check-mumbai-station-construction-details-here-3556091/ |access-date=23 July 2024 |website=Financialexpress |language=en |archive-date=23 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723002548/https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways-bullet-train-project-nhsrcl-begins-construction-work-on-7-km-undersea-rail-tunnel-check-mumbai-station-construction-details-here-3556091/ |url-status=live }} === 2025 === On 20 May 2025, it was reported that the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project had achieved a significant milestone with the completion of 300 kilometres of viaducts. The project utilises advanced construction techniques, notably the [[Incremental launch|Full Span Launching Method (FSLM)]], which accelerates construction up to ten times faster than traditional methods. A total of 6,455 full-span and 925 span units have been employed in building the viaducts. Complementing these efforts are dedicated casting yards and workshops across India, contributing to the infrastructure. Beyond the viaducts, substantial work is underway on foundations, pier construction, and girder casting.{{Cite web |last=Devadasan |first=K. P. |date=20 May 2025 |title=300 km of viaducts completed for Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project |url=https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/india/300-km-of-viaducts-completed-for-mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train-project-1.500133677 |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema |language=en}} The physical progress according to the monthly project monitoring flash report of the [[Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation]] (MoSPI) for November 2025 was 56%.{{Cite web |title=Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Big Update: Project reaches 56 percent completion, 508-km corridor likely to be operational from… |url=https://www.india.com/business/mumbai-ahmedabad-bullet-train-railway-minister-ashwini-vaishnaw-rajdhani-express-duronto-tejas-shatabdi-express-indian-railways-irctc-8291095/ |access-date=2026-02-03 |website=www.india.com |language=en}} === 2026 === In January 2026, Railway Minister, [[Ashwini Vaishnaw]], explained the first operational section will be from Surat to Bilimora and would open by 15 August 2027. This would be followed by the Vapi to Surat, Vapi to Ahmedabad and Thane to Ahmedabad sections, followed by the full line from Mumbai to Ahmedabad by 2029. In March 2026, after spending 53% of the original estimated cost, it was reported that the final price of the project had risen 83%. Supposedly, the increase largely stemmed from delays in land acquisition negotiations, during which time the land value appreciated. The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High Speed Rail Corridor (Mumbai–Ahmedabad HSR) is an under-construction high-speed rail line, which will connect Mumbai, Maharashtra, the financial hub of India, with Ahmedabad, the largest city in the state of Gujarat. When completed, it will be India's first high-speed rail line, with a design speed of 350 km/h (215 mph), and the project will include a 353 km-long (219 mi) viaduct, which will be the longest bridge in the world.
The line is being developed by the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Indian Railways, the Ministry of Railways, and the Government of India. The line will use Shinkansen technology from Japan, including rolling stock, signalling and design standards – with technology transfer to support the Make in India programme.
After delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, construction commenced in February 2021, when the NHSRCL began to pour concrete to cast the corridor's first pillar. An initial section between Surat and Bilimora in Gujarat, is planned to open for service on 15 August 2027, with the full line to open by 2029.
